newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway energy minister to take over finance - media.
newsitem.headline: Norway energy minister to take over finance - media.

text.p: Norwegian Industry and Energy Minister Jens Stoltenberg will succeed Sigbjoern Johnsen as finance minister in a new Labour party minority government being sworn in later on Friday, the domestic media reported.
The Norwegian press, radio and television reports said the 18-member cabinet due to be presented at 1 p.m. (1100 GMT) by Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland contained seven new names.

Special U.N. envoy Terje Roed Larsen, Norway's troubleshooter in the Middle East peace process, was expected to return home to head a newly created ministry for national planning and reforms of the state administration, according to the reports.
Political commentators said they expected Bjoern Tore Godal to remain as foreign minister.

Jagland's team will succeed the 18-member cabinet led by Gro Harlem Brundtland, who surprisingly announced on Wednesday that she was resigning as prime minister to give the party a fresh start for next year's elections.

"We are getting both experience and renewal (in the new cabinet)," Jagland told reporters after paying a visit to King Harald in the Royal Palace. He declined to confirm the media reports on the new administration.

Brundtland, 57, who has dominated Norwegian politics for 15 years, was to due to resign formally with her 18-member government, which includes seven women, at a regular cabinet meeting at the Royal Palace in Oslo.
Another meeting would follow at which Jagland, 46, who as party leader has been groomed four years to become premier, takes over and presents his government.
Brundtland said she was quitting before a Labour Party congress next month so that the party could devote its time entirely to its programme and a general election in September 1997.
Jagland has said he was planning no shift of economic or any other policy. But newspapers said he could make major cabinet changes to stamp his mark on the government.
Friday's media reports said finance minister Johnsen, who has been criticised by the opposition and industry on a series of issues, was expected to become an ordinary member of parliament.
parliamentarian Tom Thoresen was expected to replace Jagland as parliamentary speaker for the Labour Party.

Stoltenberg, whose boyish charm and management of the country's oil wealth has earned him widespread popularity in opinion polls, would as finance minister manage a state budget projected to show a surplus of 40.9 billion crowns ($6.35 billion) in 1997.
The government is under pressure from the opposition right and left of centre to increase expenditure before the budget is finally adopted in December. ($1=6.445 Norwegian Crown)
